meta.tagline: A rock-carved fairytale under the shadow of balloons

overview.title: Welcome to Cappadocia
overview.intro: Cappadocia is not a city but a geological fairytale: fairy chimneys sculpted from volcanic ash over millions of years, churches carved into cliffs, ancient refuge cities sinking eight floors underground. At dawn the sky fills with hundreds of balloons; at dusk the valleys burn red. Goreme, Uchisar, Urgup and Avanos are the towns of this tale — each telling its own chapter with cave hotels, pottery workshops and wine cellars. Time here flows on a geological scale; you merely lend it two or three of your days.

local_word.definition: 'Fairy chimney' — capped stone towers carved from volcanic tuff by wind and rain: Cappadocia's signature. Folk tales say fairies lived inside them, hence the name. Every valley's chimneys have their own character: many-capped in Pasabag, tall and slender in Love Valley.

rules.title: Give the balloons at least two days
rules.description: Balloons answer to the wind, and cancellation is an everyday fact here: come for one night and you leave your flight to luck. Allow two or three mornings — if the first is cancelled, the second saves you. Even if you don't fly, be on a hilltop at sunrise to watch.

rules.title: Walk the valleys, don't just look at them
rules.description: Cappadocia is not a place to see through a bus window: the rock churches of Rose Valley, the stream of Ihlara, the sunset of Kizilcukur only open up on foot. Put at least one valley hike into each day — the trails are short, the views are generous.

rules.title: Go underground, don't just look from above
rules.description: The underground cities of Derinkuyu and Kaymakli sink eight levels down: ventilation shafts, wine cellars, rolling stone doors. To understand Cappadocia you must go below the surface once — don't fear the narrow passages, the marked route is safe.

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: English widely spoken in the region

tip.label: The Cappadocia philosophy
tip.text: The day here is built on two golden hours: balloon-filled sunrise and valley sunset. Fill the space between with museums, pottery and wine — retreating to your cave hotel in the midday heat is part of the program, not a break from it.

transport.title: Getting Around the Valleys
transport.intro: Two airports feed the region; minibuses link the towns, but the freedom of the valleys lives behind a steering wheel or in a tour van.

items.title: Arriving from the airports
items.description: Nevsehir (NAV) is 40 minutes away, Kayseri (ASR) an hour: shared shuttle transfers run from both to the hotels. Book the transfer with your flight — for late-night arrivals it's the only option.

items.title: Town-to-town minibuses
items.description: Minibuses circle between Goreme, Uchisar, Urgup and Avanos all day: cheap and practical. Evening services end early — plan your after-sunset return in advance.

items.title: Rental car and scooter
items.description: The freest option for valley trailheads, underground cities and far points like Ihlara: roads are quiet, parking is easy. Scooter and ATV rental is everywhere in Goreme — come prepared for dust and sun.

items.title: The color-coded tours
items.description: The Green Tour covers Ihlara and Derinkuyu, the Red Tour circles Goreme's surroundings: a tidy solution if you have no car. Small-group tours include lunch — a guide's geology stories double the scenery.

items.title: Valley trails
items.description: The Rose Valley, Kizilcukur, Love Valley and Pigeon Valley trails start on foot from the towns: waymarks fade in places, so download an offline map. Early morning or the cool of late afternoon is hiking's golden hour.

callout.label: Balloon morning logistics
callout.text: Balloon flights start before sunrise: your hotel pickup lands between 04:30 and 05:30. You're back for breakfast after the flight — don't overload that day; a midday nap is the natural sequel to a balloon morning.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Cappadocia choosing a hotel means choosing a town: balloon-view Goreme, castle-view Uchisar, vineyard-cellared Urgup, mansion-lined Mustafapasa.

local_word.definition: 'Cave hotel' — a hotel with rooms carved into the rock: Cappadocia's lodging signature. Hollows that served as homes, stables and monasteries for centuries are now fireplace suites — the walls stay cool in summer, warm in winter, and you watch the morning balloons from the terrace.

items.name: Goreme
items.description: The town directly beneath the balloons: cave-hotel terraces open onto the world's most famous sunrise. The widest choice of restaurants and tours — central, but lively in season.

items.name: Uchisar
items.description: At the foot of the castle rock, the region's highest point: stone mansion hotels look down over the valleys. Five minutes to Goreme, one notch quieter — the town for view devotees.

items.name: Urgup
items.description: A settled town of wine cellars and stone mansions: its restaurant scene is the region's most ambitious. Close to the balloon launch fields by car — a balanced base for lovers of town life.

items.name: Ortahisar
items.description: A town around its castle rock that still lives by farming: lemon storage caves, old stone lanes, coffeehouses far from the tourist eye. For those who want Cappadocia's everyday face.

items.name: Mustafapasa
items.description: Formerly Sinasos: a town like an open-air museum with carved Greek mansions, churches and a silent square. Away from the crowds, high on elegance — they call it a second-visit town; come on your first.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Cappadocia flies in all four seasons; spring and autumn are the golden balance, and a snow-covered fairy chimney in winter is a different fairytale altogether.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Green of the Valleys
items.subtitle: Spring · Blossoming valleys, clear flight mornings
items.description: The valleys turn green, apricot trees blossom, and the hiking trails live their finest season. Flying weather is good, the crowds are thinner than summer — the season of photographers and hikers.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: On May mornings the valleys look emerald from the balloon basket — the most colorful flight window of the year. Dawn is chilly: board in layers, you'll warm up with the sunrise.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Long Days
items.subtitle: Summer · Hot middays, cool cave rooms
items.description: Days are long, the flight calendar is full, evenings are terrace dinners. The midday sun is harsh in the valleys — build your program around morning and late afternoon, and leave noon to the coolness of your cave hotel. The night sky is a star map.

callout.label: Midday note
callout.text: A valley hike at summer noon is punishing: shade is scarce and the rock radiates heat. Schedule walks for 07:00–10:00 and after 17:00 — the same trail is two different climates.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Harvest Light
items.subtitle: Autumn · Grape harvest, golden valleys
items.description: The grape harvest begins in September, the valleys turn gold, and the light works in photography's service. The weather is balanced and the flight rate high — this is Cappadocia's most mature season.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In mid-October, go to the Kizilcukur sunset: the vines have yellowed and the red rock catches fire. Bring a bottle of local Emir wine — the valley tells you the rest.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Snowy Fairy Chimneys
items.subtitle: Winter · Snow-covered valleys, fireside cave nights
items.description: When snow falls, Cappadocia becomes another planet: white-capped fairy chimneys with colorful balloons above them. Hotels are calm, prices soften, and a fireplace cave room is at its most delicious. Come prepared for cold — the scenery repays it with interest.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: Balloons over snow is the rarest view of the year: cancellations rise in winter, so allow a three-or-four-night window. Even without a morning flight, a snowy Rose Valley walk rescues the day.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Cappadocian table comes from the earth: kebab cooked in a clay pot, soup from the tandoor, Emir grapes from the vineyard — all ripened in rock-carved cellars.

local_word.definition: 'Pottery kebab' — meat and vegetables slow-cooked for hours in a clay jug sealed with dough, cracked open at the table. It's the handshake between Avanos pottery and Cappadocian cooking — the cracking is the show, the flavor belongs to the slow fire.

items.name: Testi kebab
items.description: Meat sealed in a clay jug and cooked for hours over embers: the jug is cracked at your table and the steam rises. A true testi house seals the jug to order — ask when you walk in, because a good testi cannot be rushed.
items.tag: Cracked at the table · sealed to order

items.name: Tandoor soups and beans
items.description: Dishes that cook overnight in an earthen oven are this kitchen's foundation: tandoor white beans, wedding soup with lentils. The most honest answer to a cold valley evening — look for a village lokanta.
items.tag: From the earthen oven · village lokanta

items.name: Emir grape wines
items.description: Emir, the native white grape of the volcanic soil, is the signature of these vineyards: mineral, fresh, made to be drunk in a stone cellar. Do a tasting in the cellars of Urgup and around — ask for a local cheese plate alongside.

items.name: Manti with pastirma
items.description: Neighboring Kayseri's heritage is honored at this table: tiny dumplings lined up on the spoon, with a plate of pastirma and sucuk beside. The 'forty manti to a spoon' claim is taken seriously around here.
items.tag: Kayseri heritage · counted by the spoon

items.name: Village breakfast and gozleme
items.description: A vineyard-house breakfast: village cheese, apricot jam, tandoor bread and gozleme off the griddle. The long breakfast after a balloon morning is this land's reward system.
items.tag: Post-balloon reward · hot off the griddle

items.name: Pumpkin seeds and apricot sweets
items.description: Nevsehir is the capital of the pumpkin seed: the crackling snack of every table. For dessert, candied pumpkin comes with tahini and dried apricots with walnuts — the earth's sweet summary.

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: Balloon-view terrace restaurants write the view into the bill: the true version of the same testi kebab costs half as much on a Goreme back street or in an Ortahisar village lokanta. Take the view with your coffee; set your table where the locals go.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the Goreme Open Air Museum; these six are the tale's less-read pages.

items.name: Kizilcukur (Red Valley)
items.description: Named for red cliffs that blaze in the setting sun: the trail winds through vineyards and hides rock churches with grape-vine frescoes. Enter an hour before sunset — the valley slowly turns to embers.

items.name: Cavusin
items.description: A quiet settlement between Goreme and Avanos, at the foot of an abandoned cliff village: the Church of St. John the Baptist carved into the basalt face is among the region's oldest. Tour buses stop for five minutes — you go slow.

items.name: Mustafapasa (Sinasos)
items.description: An old Greek town of carved stone mansions, frescoed churches and a silent square: the finest stonework hides in the door lintels. One coffeehouse break is enough to tell you this place's soul.

items.name: Ihlara Valley
items.description: A lush green canyon a hundred meters deep: the trail along the Melendiz stream is full of frescoed rock churches with running water for a soundtrack. The exact opposite of Cappadocia's arid image — cool, watered, green.

items.name: Ortahisar
items.description: A town at the foot of a giant castle rock that still lives by farming: lemon storage caves carved into the rock, old stone lanes, a local coffeehouse on the square. This is everyday Cappadocia behind the tourist showcase.

items.name: Avanos workshops
items.description: The red clay of the Kizilirmak river has been shaped here for millennia: Hittite forms still spin on the master's kick wheel. Sit at the wheel yourself — the clay collapses in your hands, the master smiles, and the second try is always better.

callout.label: Valley strategy
callout.text: Cappadocia's secret is clock management: museums at noon, valleys in the morning and late afternoon, Kizilcukur at sunset. The tour buses circulate from 10:00 to 16:00 — flow against them and the fairytale is yours.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Even a fairytale land has a showcase; know these four games and you'll live Cappadocia properly.

items.name: The one-morning balloon plan
items.description: Balloons obey wind cancellations: arrive for a single night and if the morning is cancelled, you go home unflown, consoled by a refund.
items.instead: Allow at least two mornings, ideally three; book the flight for the first so a cancellation has a backup. Choose a licensed operator and ask the basket size — a smaller basket means a better view.

items.name: The photoshoot-tour trap
items.description: 'Sunrise photo tours' with flying dresses and vintage jeeps sell at social-media prices; queueing on a crowded terrace overshadows the experience itself.
items.instead: For the same view, climb any hill or hotel terrace at sunrise — the balloons fly in the same sky for everyone. If you want photos, pick a quiet valley ridge.

items.name: The pre-cooked testi kebab
items.description: On some tourist menus, 'testi kebab' is pre-cooked food transferred into a jug: the show is there, the slow cooking is not.
items.instead: Choose places that seal the jug to order — needing to phone a few hours ahead is the good sign. A village lokanta with tandoor dishes is the same earth's honest flavor too.

items.name: ATV and horse-tour crowds
items.description: In the late afternoon the valleys drown in the dust of ATV convoys; a 'sunset horse tour' can turn into a caravan of fifty.
items.instead: Instead of an ATV, take an early-morning valley walk; if you want to ride, pick a stable that runs small groups and ask for the sunrise session. The valley's soundtrack should be wind, not engines.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Cappadocia the measure of a good experience is distance from the crowd: rise early for sunrise, rest at noon, descend into a valley in the late afternoon. Keep one spare morning in your calendar — in this land, flexibility is worth more than the best ticket.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From balloon dawn to crimson sunset

steps.title: Balloon morning
steps.description: At sunrise you're either in a basket or on a hill: hundreds of balloons rise at once. If you're not flying, watch from the ridges above Goreme — unforgettable either way.

steps.title: Long village breakfast
steps.description: The post-balloon reward: tandoor bread, village cheese, apricot jam, gozleme off the griddle. Don't hurry — this is the calmest hour of the day.

steps.title: Goreme Open Air Museum
steps.description: Frescoed rock churches and monastery hollows: pay the separate ticket for the Dark Church, it's worth it. Leave before the crowds swell.

steps.title: Uchisar Castle and lunch
steps.description: Climb the region's highest rock: the valleys lie at your feet. Lunch among the stone mansions on the way down — save the testi kebab for tonight.

steps.title: Pigeon Valley walk
steps.description: The trail descending from Uchisar to Goreme: rock walls carved with dovecotes and the late-afternoon light. An hour's descent with generous views.

steps.title: Kizilcukur sunset
steps.description: The hour the red cliffs catch fire: find a ridge among the vineyards and sit. At dinner your sealed clay jug awaits — the day closes with its crack at the table.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Balloons, underground and a canyon — the whole tale

steps.title: Classic Cappadocia
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: balloon dawn, the open-air museum, Uchisar, Pigeon Valley, Kizilcukur sunset.

steps.title: Underground and the south
steps.description: Morning descent into the Derinkuyu or Kaymakli underground city; noon among Mustafapasa's Greek mansions and silent square; late afternoon at Ortahisar's castle rock and local coffeehouse; evening Emir wine tasting in an Urgup cellar.

steps.title: Canyon and clay
steps.description: Morning walk along the stream in Ihlara Valley (pausing at frescoed churches); a short stop at the Agzikarahan caravanserai on the way back; late afternoon in an Avanos pottery workshop — sit at the wheel and pull your own souvenir from Kizilirmak clay.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: The Central Anatolian manner is warm and generous; these five phrases open doors from cave hotel to pottery workshop.

items.meaning: 'Welcome' — the reply is 'hoş bulduk'; say it and a smile is guaranteed
The word of invitation — over tea, at the table, at the workshop door; accept, the hospitality is serious
'Enjoy your meal' — the phrase you'll hear after the jug is cracked; opens and closes the table
'Health to your hands' — to the cook and the potter alike; the most precious thank-you in a land of handwork
'Very beautiful' — in the balloon basket, on the valley ridge, at the cellar tasting; the two words you'll use most

checklist.completion_message: The tale is complete! You've lived the land of fairy chimneys the way it deserves!
